name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Deborah Ross running with large financial advantage
Republican challenger has shown no fundraising or outside support
Markets price Ross at ~94% to win
model.rationale: A D+17 district with an incumbent who has raised $1.7 million against a Republican with no reported fundraising leaves little evidence of competitiveness, and prediction markets agree. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Ross win.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or major outside spending against Ross would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross seeks another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She enters the general election with roughly $1.3 million on hand and no outside groups opposing her, while Republican Eugene Douglass has reported no fundraising and no outside backing. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets, which price Ross near 94 percent. A double-digit Democratic margin is the most likely outcome, with low risk of an upset.
